nodes.name: Mutation creates variation
nodes.statement: New genetic variation arises from random mutations, which occur without regard to whether they help the organism.

nodes.name: Sex shuffles genes
nodes.statement: Sexual reproduction recombines existing alleles into new combinations in every generation.

nodes.name: Variation
nodes.statement: Individuals in a population differ in traits such as size, color and behavior.

nodes.name: Heredity
nodes.statement: Many traits are passed from parents to offspring through genes, so offspring tend to resemble their parents.

nodes.name: Overproduction
nodes.statement: Most species produce far more offspring than can survive. A single female cod can release millions of eggs in a season.

nodes.name: Limited resources
nodes.statement: Food, space and mates are limited, so no population can grow without bound.

nodes.name: Struggle for existence
nodes.statement: Because more offspring are born than resources can support, many die before they reproduce.

nodes.name: Differential reproduction
nodes.statement: Individuals whose traits suit their environment better tend, on average, to survive longer and leave more offspring.

nodes.name: Fitness
nodes.statement: In evolution, fitness is an individual's expected number of offspring that survive to reproduce, compared with others in the population.

nodes.name: Allele frequencies shift
nodes.statement: When carriers of an allele leave more offspring, that allele becomes more common in the next generation.

nodes.name: Natural selection
nodes.statement: Natural selection is the change in a population's heritable traits over generations, caused by differences in survival and reproduction.

nodes.name: Fitness depends on environment
nodes.statement: A trait is an advantage only in a particular environment. The same trait can become a handicap when conditions change.

nodes.name: Selection is not random
nodes.statement: Mutation is random, but selection is not. It consistently favors the variants that reproduce best in the current environment.

nodes.name: Cumulative selection
nodes.statement: Selection builds complex traits step by step, because each small improvement becomes the starting point for the next.

nodes.name: Adaptation
nodes.statement: Over many generations, selection produces traits that fit organisms to their surroundings, such as the white winter coat of an Arctic hare.

nodes.name: Eyes evolved gradually
nodes.statement: Complex eyes can evolve through small steps, from light-sensitive patches to cups to lensed eyes. Each stage still works today in some living animal.

nodes.name: Populations evolve
nodes.statement: Individuals do not evolve during their lifetimes. Populations evolve as allele frequencies change across generations.

nodes.name: No foresight
nodes.statement: Selection acts only on present reproductive success, so it cannot prepare a species for future needs.

nodes.name: Imperfect designs
nodes.statement: Each step must work at the time, so evolution yields workable rather than ideal designs. The vertebrate retina has its nerve wiring in front of the light-sensitive cells.

nodes.name: Peppered moths
nodes.statement: In industrial Britain, dark peppered moths became common on soot-blackened trees where birds found pale moths more easily. Pale moths returned once air pollution fell.

nodes.name: Antibiotic resistance
nodes.statement: When an antibiotic kills most bacteria in an infection, the few resistant ones survive and multiply, so resistance spreads quickly.

nodes.name: Galápagos finch beaks
nodes.statement: After a drought in 1977 on Daphne Major, medium ground finches with deeper beaks survived better because mostly large, hard seeds remained. The next generation had deeper beaks on average.

nodes.name: Sexual selection
nodes.statement: Traits that improve mating success can spread even when they hurt survival, as with the peacock's long, heavy tail.

nodes.name: Artificial selection
nodes.statement: Breeders who choose which animals or plants reproduce can change a species dramatically, as with the many breeds of pigeon and dog.

nodes.name: Genetic drift
nodes.statement: In small populations, allele frequencies also change by pure chance, regardless of fitness.

nodes.name: Speciation
nodes.statement: When two populations are separated and face different conditions, they can diverge until they no longer interbreed.

nodes.name: Common descent
nodes.statement: Repeated splitting of populations over billions of years means all known living things descend from a common ancestor.
